items.title: The most annoying questgivers in PC games
items.summary:
Moira Brown gets a bad rap. Fallout 3's most chipper NPC, the Minnesotan menace is an inventor who sends you out on fact-finding missions to investigate the many dangers of the Wasteland. That means she puts you in harm's way quite a lot, which many players hate her for. Others just hate her voice.

I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3. Plus she gives you an armored Vault suit just for starting her questline, and the Wasteland Survival Guide she writes with your help goes on to be a useful item in both New Vegas and Fallout 4. 

What I'm saying is, there are plenty of videogame questgivers much more annoying than Moira Brown. All of the ones below, for starters. And if you disagree, you're a big meanie.

Zero Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas 

Rockstar loves to make us sit through cutscenes where our protagonist agrees to help out some of the most annoying people alive. Zero isn't alone—in GTA: San Andreas, he's got wannabe MC/janitor OG Loc for competition—but he is the winner for absolute worst. 

Zero's the owner of a remote-control car shop at war with a rival called Berkley. He's a shrill parody nerd who shrieks dialogue like, "Curse you, Berkley, curse you!" Zero's most annoying mission is Supply Lines, where you pilot a model biplane to shoot Berkley's delivery drivers. items.title: Planeswalker, Netflix's Magic: The Gathering animated series, will have a different art style for each plane
items.summary:
Netflix's Magic: The Gathering series was initially announced in 2019 with the MCU's Russo Brothers at the helm, though they left a couple of years later thanks to the all-purpose "creative differences". That was all we heard until 2024 until Brandon Routh, who had been cast as planeswalker Gideon Jura, casually mentioned in an unrelated interview that the project had been binned.

Netflix announced soon after that actually the animated series was a go, now with Terry Matalas of Star Trek: Picard and the 12 Monkeys TV series as its head showrunner, with a teaser image showing pyromancer Chandra and leonin Ajani Goldmane silhouetted against a red sky.

Now, a mere seven years after the first reveal, there's a "sneak peek" trailer with a bunch of excited Wizards of the Coast staff, art labeled "early development", and a few seconds of Ajani and Chandra doing their stuff. 

The most intriguing part is when, over a montage of 3D props including a car that looks like an art deco Batmobile from New Capenna, executive producer and supervising director Patrick Osborne says, "All the planes exist in their own pocket universe. That comes with culture, design language, architecture, and we're even making the film-making style different depending on where it is."

That's a good idea. An animated series with different art styles for each plane the characters travel to would be a great way of representing Magic, a card game where every artist gets to put their own spin on how things look. "Each one of these cards is this window into this incredible world," Matalas says in the trailer.…

items.title: WoW: Forever dungeon mobs no longer give EXP if they're trivial for anyone in the party
items.summary:
It's been something of a rollercoaster watching Blizzard tweak the experience rewards players can expect from dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever. They've always been a reliable way to get oodles of experience and fat loots, but in Forever, the goal has seemingly been to ensure they're more of a supplement to regular questing and exploration.

Initially, mob experience values were nerfed pretty hard to compensate for a boost in quest experience, meaning that you'd get diminishing returns for spamming one dungeon over and over. Later, dungeon enemy experience was buffed by a lot, but not back to its pre-nerf value. 

In a hotfix released yesterday , dungeon experience was tweaked yet again: "Killing enemies in dungeons now awards zero experience to all party members if the level of the enemy is trivial to the level of one or more of the party members," the note reads.

A mob is considered trivial in World of Warcraft when it's a significantly lower level than you (the exact threshold changes based on your level)—you'll know an enemy is trivial to your character when its level is displayed in a gray font.

This change seems aimed at higher-level players boosting their friends or a group of paying customers through instances, potentially offsetting the experience nerfs by clearing the dungeon and its quests much faster.

items.title: Is the game funny, or just the players? Jackbox CEO says they get 'a lot of false positives' with a staff of comedy writers
items.summary:
Social improv games like those in Jackbox 's Party Packs can have vastly different vibes depending on who you're playing with. Meemaw isn't likely to appreciate the phrase "glup shitto" the way your PC gaming friends will, and those sorts of high-variance dynamics are something Jackbox Games has to stay acutely aware of, according to CEO Mike Bilder. 

"I mean we do a ton [of testing] internally, but then as games get greenlit, we'll bring in external groups," Bilder told PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield in a recent interview. "We want to make sure that we're not just local-biased with our own opinions on things. We want to make sure these games are playing well."

Something that makes it especially hard to tell whether a game is funny or they're just having a good session is the fact that they work with comedy writers—people who can make a boring game seem funny just by cracking jokes while they play.

"We get a lot of false positives because we have such funny people here that work in the office, and they make games shine," said Bilder. "No matter what the concept is, you're gonna laugh, or the way they're hosting or emceeing the game, the pitch is hilarious, and it's like, can the game do that? Or is it just [studio creative director Arnie Niekamp]? Arnie's funny … a lot of times it is just Arnie."

In the same interview, Bilder also commented on generative AI . "The people are what make this product," he said. "The comedy, the writing, and the art, all that is done by people, and we have no intention of changing that."
items.t: Is the game funny, or just the players? Jackbox CEO says they get 'a lot of false positives' with a staff of comedy writers

His updated thoughts on the matter follow years of work and months of fan organizing, and although he and director Steven Soderbergh have almost nothing to show for it, he's still pretty fired up about how it all went down.

"For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a Star Wars film," Driver said. "What are we debating? It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written."

We first learned about The Hunt for Ben Solo, a Skywalker Saga follow-up that explored a potential future for its title character, when Driver called it one of the "coolest scripts" he had "ever been a part of" late last year. items.title: GTA 6 Will Do Something the Franchise Has Never Done Before: Encourage Empathy
items.summary:
Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe talked about how next week's Grand Theft Auto changes the formula the series is known for during an interview with The Guardian (via @GameRoll_ ). Jason and Lucia will surely be able to cause a fair amount of chaos when players take control in Vice City, but in a post- Red Dead Redemption 2 world, they'll have the freedom to be kind, too.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA – at least up until now, it has been," Nelson said. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."

Games like GTA 5 have given players playgrounds and characters that can maximize the mayhem. Trevor, one of that game's three protagonists, is a great example of this chaotic energy, but in GTA 6, there doesn't seem to be a direct equivalent. Sure, Rockstar's trademark tone and instantly recognizable characters can be seen all over what few trailers we've received thus far, but everything seems a bit more grounded, too.

Falling in line with this is the news that GTA 6 will feature a world that might actually reward those who take the citizens of Leonida into consideration. Of course, that doesn't mean those who prefer to wreak havoc won't be able to play their way, too. items.title: 40% of game developers use generative AI according to a new report, but more than half reckon the technology has a negative impact on the games industry

Use of generative AI remains one of the most contentious topics in the games industry. Developers who see a bright new future in the tech have increasingly clashed with those concerned by the ethical , artistic , and labour implications tools like ChatGPT and Claude Opus bring to the medium. The divisive nature of the subject was starkly revealed in a new report, which calculated that 40% of game developers are actively using generative AI, while more than half of developers believe LLMs and agentic coding tools have a negative impact on the industry.

These were the conclusions of the latest State of the Game Industry report from the Game Developer's Conference (via Eurogamer ). The report surveyed over 2,600 respondents from all corners of the industry. Of those surveyed, 40% of respondents said they used generative AI as part of their job, a slight increase from 36% from last year .

Of those surveyed, the report found that older professionals were more likely to use generative AI, with 54% of workers over 45 stating they use the tech. The report also states that men were more likely to use AI tools than women, and that indie developers were less likely to use it than studios working on premium, free-to-play, and mobile-exclusive games.

Among those who have embraced generative AI, the most common use of it was for research and brainstorming. Nearly three-quarters of AI advocates said they use it for this function, while over half (56%) said they use it for code generation and debugging. Use of generative AI seems to drop sharply for tasks viewed as being more creative,…

Speaking to FRVR , Andersson explained that having satisfying firearms in The Great Circle was "non-negotiable" as "we have a lot of people at Machine[Games] that love guns".

Since MachineGames wanted The Great Circle to be true to Spielberg's films, they needed guns to be a part of Indy's toolset but not the default response to every problem. And yet, from a different perspective, it actually would get made… as a bunch of other, quite famous films. We’re talking Gremlins. We’re talking Poltergeist. And we’re talking E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial .

“It was a dream team of people working on this thing. It was going to be a horror movie about these evil aliens, or mischievous aliens, that come to this rural farmstead and really mess with this family – they really fuck with this family,” explains movie journalist and author Max Evry, who just released a book about the film called Stranded on Earth: How Night Skies Became E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial .

The first reference to AI comes midway through the letter: "While we previously validated game systems only after implementing them manually, we now utilize AI to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," it states. The studio immediately clarified, though, that AI "serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity," and that gameplay and content development "remain fully driven by our development team."

In an announcement posted today on Steam, developer GFAGames said further work on the game and continued operation of its servers requires more money, and it just doesn't have any.

"Over the past few months, we have been in talks with existing and potential partners about investment and new ways of working together that would allow us to preserve the project and the team," the studio wrote. 

"We were unable to agree on the funding needed to continue the project. The studio no longer has sufficient funds of its own to continue development and keep the servers running."

Pioner looked promising when it turned up at the PC Gaming Show in 2021: A mash-up of Stalker, Metro, and Escape From Tarkov that featured both a singleplayer campaign and online co-op and PvP survival action, all of it built around late Soviet-era technology. 

It launched into early access in December 2025 and worked its way to a peak concurrent player count of 1,686 on Steam a few months later—not huge, but far from catastrophic, and trending in the right direction.

As we've covered in previous lectures, everyone is Franklin . This is disconcerting. Even more disconcerting is that, as of today, all the Franklins now have a singular object of cathexis: Franklin.

Uh, that is to say, Franklin Prime: me. I have installed Look At Me , a Grand Theft Auto 5 mod whose purpose is to make you the centre of attention wherever you go and wherever you teleport. In the street, crowds round on you, fixing you with a silent stare as though they know everything you've ever done, everything you will ever do. Even parkour does not mollify them.

(Image credit: Rockstar) It turns your every step in GTA 5 into something paranoid and faintly Lynchian. I am being gangstalked by myself, and all the while wars rage, cars float overhead, and the world in general spins out of control on every axis. Sometimes it finds new axes, and they're all irreparably hosed.

Look At Me does not appear to affect NPCs who have been placed with a purpose. Or it sometimes doesn't, anyway. My bodyguard? Unpredictable. Sometimes he will stand stock-still, and join the masses in gawping at me. Other times, he couldn't care less. My wife never looks at me; this is troubling.

It's a bold and unnerving new world, and one that I suppose is much harder to commit unwitnessed crimes in. Does anyone know how to make my wife look at me…

items.title: Chipmaking giant TSMC discovers major employee data leak—reports say info was up for sale for three bitcoin on shady forums
items.summary:
TSMC, the juggernaut that produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips, has discovered a data leak said to contain over 46,000 employee records, according to Seeking Alpha .

The company made a Form 6-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday, stating: "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised."

The company says the info has been verified to match data "stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," although said provider is not named. TSMC says it has informed those impacted by the breach and is providing support, and has also engaged with the cloud service vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to "ascertain the facts and take necessary actions."

Taiwanese outlet United Daily News reports that hackers were allegedly offering the employee records on an underground forum for the princely sum of three bitcoin, in exchange for 6.9 GB worth of private data. 

The outlet also says that, "according to information online" (via machine translation), hackers were also selling what appears to be TSMC employee data on other forums, releasing a small sample which is said to contain a vast array of personal details, including national ID numbers, addresses, and banking information. 

(Image credit: TSMC) TSMC has confirmed in its statement that the leaked data is unrelated to the company's operations, or customer-related information.…

items.title: Intel takes massive chunk out of AMD's desktop CPU market share in unexpected turnaround - may be due to the red team's dominance in gaming chips, weirdly
items.summary:
Intel appears to have gained market share from AMD in a rare turnaround for the company. The red team's chips have been in the lead in performance and popularity for many years now, and frankly, they still are. That's what weird about this one: AMD may have lost ground because it makes the best CPUs for gaming .

The latest Q3, 2026 data from market researchers Mercury Research suggests an increase in market share for desktop CPUs of 5.1%. Now, considering AMD has fought tooth and nail for a decade to increase its share to around 35% as of Q2, 2026, dropping down to just 29.9% in the following three months marks a gargantuan lurch back towards Intel. 

Our pick for the best gaming CPU is the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , and many other AMD chips make up our recommendations. While we do recommend the Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus due to its surprisingly low price tag and plenty of cores, I wouldn't go as far as believing any Arrow Lake chip has been key to turning around Intel's fortunes among gamers. The architecture struggles to keep up with AMD's latest in gaming, and it is built on a dead-end platform—Nova Lake chips are expected soon on a different motherboard socket.

The increase in market share is almost too big to be believed, which is certainly one theory as to what's going on. A rounding error or errant data—though Mercury Research have been pretty locked in in the past. Both Intel and AMD cite their numbers when it makes them look good.

items.title: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games
items.summary:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.

When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.
